title: Shaft Tombs on the Nablus Road, Jerusalem
author: R. W. Hamilton and S. A. S. Husseini
screen_term: jerusalem (also 'nablus' in the road name; placed in Jerusalem)
location_note: Junction of Saladin Road and the Nablus Road, immediately south and south-west of the 'Tombs of the Kings'; second group about 300 m further south beside the Nablus Road. No map reference; placed by name.
notes: May 1934: seventeen rock-cut shaft tombs of four types (A-D) found in road works, twelve excavated (13-17 disturbed, covered up). Feb. 1933: four shaft tombs and a chamber tomb with sunk graves 300 m south. Gold ear-rings, glass, lamps; one coin 'perhaps Herodian' in a grave, but the excavators put the mean date in the third century AD (lamps early 3rd to 5th c.).

features.site: Saladin Road junction (17) and Nablus Road 300 m south (5)
features.subtype: rock-cut shaft tombs with slab-covered graves (types A-D), and one chamber tomb with sunk graves
features.period: Roman; mean date third century AD, objects hardly earlier than the second century (excavators)
features.quote: a group of seventeen rock-cut tombs, of Roman date, was brought
